$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Action binding extension 0.3.0 (proposal), written against Core v1.3 rev. 11 and reference files 5.2.0, with signatures 0.2.0 and anchoring 0.2.0 for a signed attachment. Binds only an implementation that says it uses this extension.
title: Action binding verification report
description: What a verifier found in a set of execution-evidence attachments, dimension by dimension, with the scope of its conclusion. There is deliberately no overall result: no dimension stands for the others, and nothing here is a legal conclusion or a Conformance Level.

attachment_count.description: The number of attachments checked. The report has one result for each, and each attachment_index from 0 to this count minus 1 appears once. There is one attachment per decision record, so no two results name the same decision_id; this can be checked only among the attachments one report covers. JSON Schema cannot compare two documents: a reader holding both checks it.

trust_policy_ref.description: The trust policy the verifier configured independently of the attachments: anchoring 0.2.0's.

trust_policy.description: Whether the policy itself was accepted: one public key, one key reference, one holder, one role; one reference, one entry (anchoring 0.2.0). A refused policy fails every issuer signature. The same object as in an anchoring, signatures or portable verification report. A verifier holding only unsigned attachments still names the policy it would use and says whether it accepts it.

signatures_attachment_digest.description: SHA-256 of the signatures 0.2.0 attachment read beside the attachments, as received, when one was: the seals carried beside and the independent timestamps over signature values come from it.

then.description: A refused policy: no issuer signature verifies.

assurance.description: Identity, authority or legal signature. An issuer's own assertion, signed or not, is never reported as verified.

time_assurance.description: Time. Verified only against a verified independent timestamp over this attachment's verified issuer signature, from the signatures attachment read beside: it shows that the signature, and so the attachment's bytes as issued, existed no later than no_later_than. It never shows when any stage happened; the stage times and sealed_at are the issuer's assertions.

source_ref.description: The authority the policy pins (its tsa_ref).

no_later_than.description: genTime plus the token's accuracy, if it states one: the time T by which the signature existed.

timestamp_index.description: The timestamp in the signatures attachment.

key_state.description: The key's state when the signature was made, as anchoring 0.2.0 defines it, with the copy's sealed_at as the stated time. time_basis says what that time rests on: stated_time is the issuer's own statement, never independent time; independent_timestamp is a verified timestamp over the signature value, from the signatures attachment read beside.

timestamp_index.description: The timestamp the time rests on, in the signatures attachment.

allOf.description: After a compromise, only an independent timestamp earlier than revoked_at establishes the time.

issuer_signature.description: The copy of the organisation's seal, as one dimension: the holder the policy names for the key issued these exact bytes under this decision_id. Verified only when the signature over the bytes the verifier built from the attachment verifies with the policy's key, in role organisation, and the key's state when it signed is verified. It attests only that the issuer recorded these claims. holder is the holder the policy gives for the key: the attachment names no issuer. certificate says that the certificate the policy pins for the key holds it (verified), or that none is pinned (not_checked): no chain to a trusted list, no revocation check. An unsigned attachment is not_checked, with the finding that it carries no signature; it is never verified. Anyone holding a signed attachment can remove issuer_signature and present it as unsigned: a relying party that needs a signed attachment requires one in its own configuration.

reference_source.description: Where the key came from: only ever the policy.

spec_index.description: The position of the specification in the attachment, from 0.

spec_digest.description: The digest the attachment states for it.

digest.description: The bytes against the stated digest.

statements.description: The summary outside the digest, against the bytes.

observed_results.description: The observed result of each attempt, carried through as the attachment records it. A missing result is reported as missing.

basis.description: The basis of the observation, as recorded. executor_observation: the executor's own word.

attachment_index.description: The position of this result's attachment in the input, from 0.

attachment_digest.description: SHA-256 of the attachment's bytes as received. Attachments are not sealed or chained, so this digest is what fixes which bytes were checked, for a reader who holds the report as the verifier issued it.

specifications.description: One result for each action specification in the attachment.

reviews.description: For each review, whether the reviewer was shown what was proposed: as_proposed, differs_from_proposal (with edited_by, the author of that change, where the attachment names them), or proposal_not_named.

executed_specifications.description: For each specification attempted, how it was reached: shown to a reviewer and approved, only through an authorised change that no reviewer was shown (and that used up a request of what it changes), only through a request resting on a standing approval (no reviewer was shown it; standing_approvals says whether it was checked against the bounds), or by none of these (unbound).

standing_approvals.description: One entry for each standing approval the attachment records, when it records any. The bounds dimension says whether the bytes matched their digest and read as well-formed bounds; a request is checked against bounds only when they are verified. requests_recorded counts the requests the attachment records as resting on the approval, not requests run. revocation says whether a revocation is recorded, never that none was given. No one is shown to have looked at any request.

record_statements.description: The stages' statements about core fields, against the decision record. not_checked when the verifier does not hold the record, when an approval names no core field (the record does not show it), or when a review_log outcome is a word the check does not know.

action_binding.description: Shown, approved, requested and attempted digests agree, or are joined by an authorised change, or each request under a standing approval is inside its verified bounds. not_checked when a request rests on bounds that could not be read, and nothing failed.

time_basis.description: The times the order was checked against.

allOf.description: No specification is reported as executed when nothing was attempted.
An unbound executed specification is a failed binding.

Bounds that are not verified leave the requests resting on them unchecked: with a request recorded on them, the binding is not verified. An approval no request rests on constrains nothing (item 13 is about the requests).
